title: A green, versatile, and facile strategy for anti-biofouling surface with ultra-high graft density polyethylene glycol

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text first states, 'The silicon substrate was immersed in 500 µl of PC solution... The pH was then adjusted to 5.5 with 0.1 M sodium hydroxide.' Later in the same section it states, 'All the pH adjustments mentioned above were made using 1 mM salt. Specifically, 1 mM hydrochloric acid and 1 mM sodium hydroxide were used for the above pH adjustments.' These two statements are mutually contradictory, giving a 100-fold discrepancy (0.1 M vs. 1 mM) for the concentration of NaOH used to adjust pH, making the described protocol internally inconsistent and unreproducible as written.

predicted_errors.error_location: Methods, grafting density calculation equation (δ = ρSΔLNA/MS)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The grafting density formula is given as δ = ρSΔLNA/MS, with S explicitly defined as 'the grafted area.' However, S appears identically in both the numerator and denominator of the equation, meaning it mathematically cancels out and has no effect on the computed value of δ. This makes the explicit definition of S as a meaningful input variable nonsensical, since the standard physical derivation of grafting density from film thickness and density (δ = ρΔL·NA/M) does not require an area term at all. As written, the equation is either redundant/incorrect or a transcription error that would not actually use the 'grafted area' as claimed.

The paper defines 'Hemolysis ratio (%) = (OD samples – OD negative) / (OD positive – OD negative)' and explicitly labels the output as a percentage. However, the formula as written only produces a fraction (a decimal ratio), not a percentage, because it omits the standard multiplication by 100 needed to convert the ratio into percent units. As presented, the formula is inconsistent with the stated '%' units.
